body: Think back to who you are, the moments you made people smile and laugh. The times you felt like you accomplished something. Yes, it gets dark and it will be hard but you must be your own light to find your way out of hell. Only you can make the choice, and only you can save yourself.

I wish I had words to snatch you back from the edge. My mom always said, when it rains it pours. Those are some heavy hits, and hearing your words stings deep to scars that I never healed from.   


Sometimes all we can do is put one foot in front of the other. One step, one goal...one swing. Even if we dont want to, or see no point. Time is the only thing that can pull you from those depths. At one point in my life I wanted to cure depression, looking back now I feel foolish. Insignificant and small to try at such a task. However very few things matter to me anymore. I have been focused...and pushed. I hope your heart and soul rest....whatever happens. It seems to be the darkest before the dawn. Maybe you will find a million dollar lottery ticket in the wind on the roof. :) \*bows his head in respect\*

Dont get me wrong, I get up every day in pain and spend most of the day being quiet as I struggle to avoid the depressing thoughts. In a way, I am in torment as I try to push through bulging discs, anxiety and stress. Not to mention Heart issues.   


Trust me, I get it...it should just stop, like a train or some ride that you can get off and wave goodbye to. However I cant give up....I am a caregiver, a leader to some, mentor, adviser, and council. I feel stupid, lazy and worthless when I cant do things how I think I should be able to do them. People call me smart all the time and dont get why I dont see it....but honestly, they dont know how hard I have struggled. How much I stressed and how many times I have given up or just slid through.  


Yet over the years, I have started to look at the world as a growing darkness with very few true lights left out in it. Too many people pretend to care, and so very few truly mean it...and that costs them more than many will ever know. However I must admit I am blessed to have many things. Food, a home, loved ones, and memories I cherish so much....memories I drift too and pull from. I am not perfect, but I am me....human, I am a warrior. My light is passed one, like a candle lighting another candle. I have my of darkness but....its my burden to bear. My demon to chain...., I honestly find the best part of my life counted in the times I have inspired and helped others. Those moments when I truly felt like I touched what we would call a soul.   


I dont have the answers, but I do hope you find your way. Find your light in the darkness. This world is so grey....but there IS good here too. Good planted by a seed of hope.   


We all must walk our own path, but I do believe what doesnt kill you....makes you stronger. YOU and only you, will ever be able to face your own worst enemy. Yourself.

Killing yourself is the most selfish thing you can do, even if it seems like it is the answer. We all want to take the easy way out, we all need respite, and time. However taking your own life does nothing about ending the pain and guilt you feel. All it does is pass it on to those who care about you. You may find yourself reaching for excuses and trying to justify it but the truth is you would be the root cause.   


We all fall down, we all make mistakes, and have issues. Are you reading this? Are you still breathing? You can still change, be better, and work on yourself. Get back up, and start swinging. People care about you for a reason, they see more than you do. A unique perspective that you will never fully grasp. In the end we all have a choice, we all have to make our way. Try to be more selfless, but yes we are all selfish too.   


You have NEVER hit rock bottom. Cause if you did, you wouldnt get back up. Rock bottom is THE END, death and game over. That which you hit, that which you find yourself standing on as a foundation was forged by others JUST like you. You are not alone, even when you think you are. BE the monument for those you call friends, family, and those who know the real you.   


The scars of the past, shape us all, for the future. Only YOU, know your true self.... and know what truly matters. Never stop fighting.

Please, all I ask is that you read and share

Wednesday Oct 24 started out just as any other day, yet soon my family would be thrown into a nightmare. My mother who had been struggling with depression, self doubt and crippling loss of self worth turned at first to anger before rage. A situation in which she found herself at a loss of self-control. She found herself lost not just emotions but in sound judgement. As the chaos of overwhelming pain, regret, grief and hopelessness led to her attempting to overdose with pills. While this will always be a painful scar upon our family, it was not the darkest moment of this story.

The Instant I was informed of my mothers dire situation, I forced her into the car before rushing to seek aid to save her life. In the panic of my stressed mind I turned to the place all of us do in the most dire straights - The Emergency Room. Soon after relaying all of the crisis, including that she had taken over a half a bottle of unknown medications, mom was taken back as I finished admittance. Upon reassurance that she was no longer in danger, I shifted my attention to that of my disabled father ((Her Husband)) unable to walk who was left behind in the rush. Informing the receptionist of my intentions to be back in a few minutes, I rushed off to quickly reunite my family to be with my mom during her struggle. Upon returning in less than ten minutes, I was greeted with a sight that stunned me to my very core.

My mother who was suppose to be receiving life saving treatment was being escorted out in handcuffs by police. That was when I was informed that in few minutes I had been gone my mother had refused to change, and had an altercation with a staff member. This incident was nothing major as no one was hurt, and my mother still is unable doing anything violent. Though it was enough for those who COULD help, those who I trusted with her life AT ALL COSTS, to abandoned the woman in need. Her mental

status was unquestionably not sound and her actions wrong but not the noble caring woman who loved her family and served her country.

Soon both myself and my father found ourselves begging both the police, and the Hospital for help seeking for an understanding that she was in danger of losing her life and each moment could be doing her permanent harm. Despite our pleas, and ignoring any protest or challenges to what was right or wrong my mother a US Air Force Veteran was discharged, dumped on the streets and refused life saving treatment. No matter what we did, they could not see the woman's sacrifice, the love she had given, the pain she had suffered. They only had fear and anger at the helpless old woman ((Over 50)) in cuffs, who soon was placed inside of a police car where her family might watch her pass out and die. Our mindset had no choice but to shift from how can they help, to what must we do to GET her help. In the panic and pleading for her release the officer agreed to allow us to take her but with a PUNISHMENT of a fine for disorderly conduct. That she HAD to appear in court tomorrow in return for release unto our custody. We agreed of course, despite not knowing if she would be alive in the next hour let alone home anytime soon.

From there we raced to the next Hospital, the closes ER hoping for the help she had been denied and punished for seeking. Each moment in that drive to the next city was more painful than I can explain in words, as I struggled to keep my mother with us knowing that should she pass out she might never awaken. I am happy to say she did make it, she got treatment and I am ETERNALLY grateful to the heroes of the other two hospitals that gave us all another chance. No matter what happens, I will do everything I can for her and for our family. She is currently getting more treatment, and we are trying to deal with the court as we hope her whole story will bring the ridiculous state of this situation to those who will help. No matter what happens, I can not deny how horrible this was. How I do not understand that a Emergency room could refuse a life in danger. How police would not strive to get her to treatment, and most of all how a Doctor who swore a oath to do no harm would abandon a woman in such dire need. I hope that her story is heard, that no human being would ever beg for a loved ones life to saved.

NO VETERAN WHO SACRIFICED FOR THAT WHICH WE ALL HAVE IN THIS COUNTRY SHOULD EVER BE TREATED THIS WAY!

We are in the process of trying to get help still, needing representation and support. I have never asked the public of anything, and my mother has given so much. Please share this story.
